title: Bivariate meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy in the browser: a tool validated against the R package mada
description: Validation archive v1.1.0 for F1000 paper 3: the allmeta DTA SROC app from allmeta v1.8.0 (commit 1cb3f8409c7af75ed41f7e1811f9c502f900fc79, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23515177). The original validation inputs, R reference code, expected values and tolerances are unchanged. The recorded 2026-10-20 provenance/run_plan-2026-10-20-release.log (lines 15-184), against 1cb3f84, reports 855/855 checks across 105 configurations (80 fits and 25 matched refusals; Moses 18/18), 53/53 paper quantities and pinned replay 855/855. Adds PR #133 extras validation for bivariate meta-regression, conditional ROC confidence/prediction regions and post-test probabilities: 195,291/195,291 checks over 27 configurations. The separate raw-scale gate passed over 3,528 configurations with 222 raw and 8 standardised out-of-tolerance configurations, all noted; maximum relative difference 1.89e-4. This is not universal numerical agreement. Negative controls passed 23/23 and oracle tests 8/8. Includes unchanged reference corpora, R generators, wrappers, local browser dependencies, checksums and reproduction instructions. R 4.6.0, mada 0.5.12, mvmeta 1.0.3; extras corpus uses metadat 1.6-0. The recorded run used Node 24.13.0 and the documented Python dependency deviations with --allow-version-mismatch; see README. FINAL_BLOBS.cmd restores and verifies the 245 release blobs before documented privacy redactions; published hashes distinguish those derivatives. The helper awaits execution by the human-side runner. Existing v1.0.0 links and validation history are retained.
